title: Prevent admission-ripple causing long-context queue amplification and KV-eviction cascades
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (notably AcmeAI and a top-ten enterprise Dedicated tenant) reported intermittent long-context tail latency and sustained throughput drops during mixed-length workloads. Root cause investigation indicates an admission-control ripple: a burst of very long-context requests triggers aggressive KV-cache eviction and admission gating that amplifies queue lengths for subsequent short requests, producing long tail latencies and cascading preemption that degrades overall throughput across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket captures the mitigation, fix, and rollout plan to stop the ripple and prevent KV eviction cascades.
repro_steps: 1) Use a mixed-length synthetic load: 10% requests with 64k token context and 90% short requests (<=128 tokens) across 20 concurrent clients. 2) Configure batching with adaptive windowing and default KV reserve at 0%. 3) Observe dispatcher admission spikes when a long-context burst enters; KV cache size drops and fewer short-request batches are admitted. 4) Symptoms: queue depth for short requests increases by 3-10x, p95/p99 latency for short requests spikes to 1-3s, throughput drops ~20-40%. Reproducible in staging with workload generator script linked in comments.
detection_telemetry: Alerts: p99_short_request_latency_alert fired thrice in 24h. Dashboards: /dashboards/scheduler/admission_ripple shows correlated spikes in kv_evictions_per_min and admitted_long_batches. Canary logs show admission_backoff events timed with KV eviction bursts. Heap of evidence collected in Runbook doc (Confluence link in comments) and Grafana snapshots attached.
impact_scope: Observed in: hosted api (multi-tenant), several Dedicated clusters (reserved pools with mixed tenants), and on-prem Private installs where KV memory is constrained. Affects latency-sensitive flows (chat UIs, inference RPCs) more than bulk embedding jobs. Customer escalations received from two customers; one requested immediate mitigation to avoid contract SLA breach.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): 1) Introduce an emergency admission_backoff window for long-context arrivals (config: admission_ripple_backoff_ms=250) to prevent immediate mass re-admission. 2) Reserve a small KV cache partition for short requests (kv_reserve_pct=12) to avoid full eviction. 3) Apply conservative admission rate cap for low-priority tenants during long-context surges. Deliver as runtime-1.19.1 patch and opt-in config in Hosted; provide hotfix diffs and operator instructions for Dedicated/Private.
fix_design: Long-term: implement admission smoothing and token-aware fairness in the dispatcher: - Track per-length token cost budget per admission window. - Preferentially schedule short requests when their predicted token-cost budget is under-utilized. - Make KV eviction decisions aware of recency and predicted re-use (pin recent short prefixes). - Expose operator knobs: admission_backoff_ms, kv_reserve_pct, token_budget_window_ms. Design doc linked in comments with pseudocode for token-budget algorithm.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary rollout on hosted non-production region (3 machines) with telemetry gates for p95/p99 short latency and kv_evictions. 2) If canary stable for 24h, promote to all hosted regions. 3) Publish hotfix package and deployment playbook for Dedicated customers; coordinate with SEs for Private on-prem upgrades. 4) For customers with strict change windows, provide manual configuration steps and backout plan. Rollout checklist included in comments.
acceptance_criteria: - p99 latency for short requests reduces to baseline within 10% under mixed-length synthetic load. - kv_eviction_rate reduces by >=60% during bursts. - No regressions on long-request throughput beyond 5% degradation. - Hotfix deployed to hosted and at least one Dedicated customer with verification signoff.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission policy logic, integration test harness with mixed-length workload generator, stress tests simulating KV eviction pressure, and end-to-end perf tests in staging with real-model kernels. Add regression tests to scheduler-e2e with deterministic replay (see ENG-70233 for deterministic replay infra).
rollback_plan: Disable admission_backoff flag and restore previous kv_reserve_pct. For Hosted, rollback by reverting canary image. For Dedicated/Private, operator instructions to revert config and restart dispatcher gracefully. Backout runbook attached.
notes: Related findings: eviction-induced stall patterns correlate strongly with small-request suppression during mixed loads; see profiling notes in comment dated 2026-03-07. We prioritized short-request preservation because customer-facing UIs were impacted. Liaised with SEs to provide per-customer mitigations (rate-limiting long-request clients) while fix is deployed.
